original_question: It is known that there exist residually finite, locally finite, characteristically simple groups with finitely many orbits under automorphisms(A. B. Apps, J. Algebra, 81(1983), 320–339). Are there any locally finite, characteristically simple groups with finitely many orbits under automorphisms that are not residually finite?
target_in_paper: Open Problem 21.39 in the section "New Problems (21st issue, 2026)"; your draft matches this entry essentially verbatim. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact problem posed in the paper: it keeps the Apps reference, the hypotheses "locally finite" and "characteristically simple," the condition of having finitely many orbits under automorphisms, and the precise existence question about failure of residual finiteness. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
missing_details: For full stand-alone clarity, introduce an explicit ambient group G and phrase the problem as an existence question about such a group.
Make explicit that "finitely many orbits under automorphisms" refers to the natural action of Aut(G) on the set G.

If complete self-containment is desired, unpack the standard terms: locally finite means every finitely generated subgroup is finite; characteristically simple means G has no nontrivial proper characteristic subgroups; not residually finite means some nontrivial element survives in no finite quotient.
Do not add extra hypotheses such as countability, finite generation, or linearity; the paper does not impose any such restrictions.
refined_question: Does there exist a group G such that every finitely generated subgroup of G is finite, G has no nontrivial proper characteristic subgroups, the natural action of Aut(G) on G has only finitely many orbits, and G is not residually finite (equivalently, some nontrivial element of G maps to the identity in every homomorphism from G to a finite group)?
justification: arXiv:1401.0300 is not a standard single-topic paper with items such as Conjecture 1.1 or Theorem 1.3; it is the Kourovka Notebook, a collection of open problems. Within it, the exact target of your draft is Problem 21.39, whose wording is essentially the same as your draft. The only real refinement needed is to make the Aut(G)-action explicit and to render the statement fully stand-alone without changing its scope. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300))
